chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abi Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام was brought a man and his wife, and her husband had committed liwat with her son from another man and had penetrated him, and the witnesses testified against him regarding that. So Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ordered concerning him, and he was struck with the sword until he was killed. And the boy was struck with less than the hadd, and he said: “Indeed, if you had been mature, I would have killed you for enabling him against yourself so that he penetrated you.”

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَا: Imam Ali عليه السلام, acting here as the judicial authority issuing the ruling
key_terms.الشُّهُودُ: the witnesses whose testimony established the act
key_terms.لِإِمْكَانِكَ إِيَّاهُ مِنْ نَفْسِكَ: for having enabled him against yourself
key_terms.مُدْرِكًا: having reached maturity or legal accountability

ai.seo_question: What punishment is mentioned in Shia hadith for an adult who commits liwat, and how is a minor treated in the ruling?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal judgment from Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام concerning liwat involving a man and his wife's son from another man. It distinguishes between the ruling on the adult perpetrator and the lesser punishment of the boy due to his not having reached maturity, while indicating the legal gravity of consent had he been mature.
